findings.description: VERIFIED: the frontend gate cannot pass without violating the spec delta. `specs/coordinator-kanban-viz/spec.md:32-37` keeps the normative scenario `Historical vendor still renders`: WHEN a card has a child agent whose agent_id suffix is `gemini` THEN that agent SHALL render in its own lane labelled `gemini`. The only test that exercises VendorSwimlanes is `apps/kanban-viz/src/__tests__/VendorSwimlanes.test.tsx`, which today carries that fixture at lines 22-23, 58, 62, 67, 72, 152 (`grep -ni gemini apps/kanban-viz/src/__tests__/VendorSwimlanes.test.tsx`). But tasks.md:246 requires `git grep -lIi gemini -- apps/kanban-viz` to list *exactly the three provenance files*, and work-packages.yaml:278 asserts `test "$(git grep -lIi gemini -- apps/kanban-viz | wc -l | tr -d ' ')" = "3"`. I ran that grep: it returns 4 files today (the 3 provenance files + VendorSwimlanes.test.tsx). To reach 3 the implementer must strip the gemini fixture, which deletes the only mechanical evidence for the `Historical vendor still renders` scenario — the scenario that exists precisely to prove D5's roster-agnostic rendering. Either the gate fails at 4 or the spec scenario goes unsatisfied. Resolution: exempt VendorSwimlanes.test.tsx from the count (expect 4, or add `':!*/VendorSwimlanes.test.tsx'`) and state in task 4.1 that the historical-vendor fixture is retained by design, alongside the 3 provenance carve-outs.

VERIFIED: `npm test -- --run` fails in this repo and will fail by construction in wp-frontend's isolated worktree, and no task or gate installs frontend dependencies. I ran `cd apps/kanban-viz && npm test -- --run` → `sh: vitest: command not found`; `ls apps/kanban-viz/node_modules` → absent. `node_modules` is gitignored, so a fresh `git worktree add` (wp-frontend declares `mode: isolated`, work-packages.yaml:268-269) starts with no dependencies at all. That command is the first clause of wp-frontend's only verification step (work-packages.yaml:278), of tasks.md:244 (checkpoint 4.3), of tasks.md:307 (task 6.2), and of wp-docs-finalize verification step 2 (work-packages.yaml:365) — four gates, none of which can reach a passing state. Resolution: prefix each frontend invocation with `npm ci --prefix apps/kanban-viz` (or add an explicit dependency-install task to Phase 4 with `npm ci` and make 4.3/6.2 depend on it).

VERIFIED: task 0.1's remediation command would break every skills gate it exists to repair. tasks.md:28-33 says add fastapi/httpx to `skills/pyproject.toml` and 're-sync `skills/.venv` via `uv sync`'. `pytest` is NOT in `skills/pyproject.toml`'s `[project] dependencies` (lines 7-16) — it lives only in the `test` optional-dependency group (lines 26-29), and the SDKs live only in `sdk` (lines 19-24). Bare `uv sync` installs no extras, so it would uninstall pytest from `skills/.venv`, after which `skills/.venv/bin/python -m pytest skills/tests -q` — the gate in task 0.3, task 3.12, task 6.2, wp-skills verification (work-packages.yaml:220) and wp-docs-finalize step 2 (work-packages.yaml:365) — cannot run at all. Evidence the venv was built with extras: `ls skills/.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages` shows `anthropic`, `google_generativeai-0.8.6`, and `pytest-9.0.3`, i.e. both optional groups are installed. The repo's own instruction is `cd skills && uv sync --all-extras` (docs/guides/python-environment.md:5). Resolution: task 0.1 must say `uv sync --all-extras`, and must state which group fastapi/httpx go into (the `test` group).

VERIFIED: four of the nine test locations task 3.1 writes against are never executed by any gate in the plan. Task 3.1 (tasks.md:149-157) explicitly lists `skills/parallel-infrastructure/scripts/tests/`, `skills/parallel-infrastructure/tests/test_vendor_diversity.py`, `skills/fix-scrub/tests/test_vendor_dispatch.py`, and `skills/autopilot/scripts/tests/test_implementation_strategy_selector.py`. None of these is under `skills/tests/`, and none appears in `skills/pyproject.toml`'s `[tool.pytest.ini_options] testpaths` (which lists `tests/parallel-infrastructure`, i.e. `skills/tests/parallel-infrastructure`, not `parallel-infrastructure/scripts/tests`). Every gate in the plan runs only `pytest skills/tests` (tasks.md:224, 305; work-packages.yaml:220, 365). I measured the gap: `skills/.venv/bin/python -m pytest skills/tests --collect-only -q` → 1249 tests collected; `pytest skills/parallel-infrastructure/scripts/tests skills/parallel-infrastructure/tests skills/fix-scrub/tests skills/autopilot/scripts/tests --collect-only -q` → a disjoint 536 tests. Those 536 are inside wp-skills' residue-grep scope (`git grep -lIi gemini -- skills ...` lists e.g. `skills/parallel-infrastructure/scripts/tests/test_review_dispatcher.py`, `skills/parallel-infrastructure/tests/test_vendor_diversity.py`, `skills/fix-scrub/tests/test_vendor_dispatch.py`), so the implementer is forced to edit them to make the grep pass, but no gate ever runs them — the classic 'edit to satisfy grep, break the assertion, ship green' path. Resolution: add `skills/*/scripts/tests/ skills/parallel-infrastructure/tests skills/fix-scrub/tests --rootdir=.` (or equivalent testpaths entries) to the wp-skills gate and to tasks 3.12 / 6.2. Note the additional collection error I hit there (`skills/parallel-infrastructure/scripts/tests/test_api_key_resolver.py: No module named 'api_key_resolver'` from repo root; and `skills/validate-feature/scripts/tests/test_migration_compat.py` errors under `--rootdir=.`) — those must be sorted in Phase 0 alongside the fastapi repair, or the newly-added gate is red from the start.

VERIFIED: the coordinator suite is red on this branch today, and Phase 0 — which exists to enumerate exactly this class of failure — does not cover it. I ran the exact gate command `agent-coordinator/.venv/bin/python -m pytest agent-coordinator/tests -q -m 'not e2e and not integration'` → `3 failed, 2027 passed, 1 skipped, 90 deselected`. The failures are `test_docker_manager.py::TestDetectRuntime::test_auto_falls_back_to_podman` (`assert detect_runtime("auto") == "podman"` → got `'docker'`), `TestStartContainer::test_successful_start` (result carries an unexpected `colima_started: True` key), and `TestStartContainer::test_compose_up_fails`. These are pre-existing, not caused by this branch — `git diff --stat origin/main...HEAD -- agent-coordinator/` is empty — and they are environment-independent: the failing test patches both `shutil.which` and `subprocess.run` (test_docker_manager.py:75-85), so the mocks fully control the code path; `colima` is not even on PATH here. They look like implementation drift (colima support added to `docker_manager.py` without updating its tests). Consequence: wp-coordinator's single verification step (work-packages.yaml:144) starts with this suite and short-circuits on its non-zero exit, so the AND-chain never reaches the residue grep, the `google-generativeai` check, or `make -n`. Task 2.10 (tasks.md:142-143), task 6.2 (tasks.md:304), and wp-docs-finalize step 2 (work-packages.yaml:365) fail for the same reason. Phase 0 lists three baseline repairs and this is a fourth. I did not verify whether CI also fails these. Resolution: add a Phase 0 task repairing (or explicitly deselecting, with a rationale) the three `test_docker_manager.py` failures, and make wp-coordinator depend on it.

VERIFIED VACUOUS GATE: the runtime-mirror check can never fail, because it greps paths git does not track. `git check-ignore -v .claude/skills .agents/skills` → `.gitignore:271:.claude/skills/` and `.gitignore:272:.agents/skills/`; `git ls-files .claude/skills | wc -l` → 0, same for `.agents/skills`. I ran the gate's own expression: `git grep -lIi gemini -- .claude/skills` exits 1 with empty output, and `test -z "$(git grep -lIi gemini -- .claude/skills .agents/skills ':!*SKILL.md')"` prints GATE PASSES VACUOUSLY. Meanwhile the real mirrors on disk DO carry live gemini references — `grep -rliI gemini .claude/skills` returns `.claude/skills/collect-transcripts/config.yaml.example` and `.claude/skills/langfuse/scripts/install-mcp.sh` (same under `.agents/skills`). So task 6.1 (tasks.md:297-299) and wp-docs-finalize verification step 2 (work-packages.yaml:365) assert 'the mirrors carry no live gemini references' with a check that is structurally incapable of reporting one — the same vacuous-gate class D8.2 was written to eliminate, reintroduced through the choice of `git grep` (correct for tracked scope inventory, wrong for gitignored mirrors). This also leaves `skill-workflow`'s `Runtime mirror drift is detected` scenario (specs/skill-workflow/spec.md:31-34), which task 6.1 cites, unverified. Related: wp-docs-finalize declares `write_allow: .claude/skills/**, .agents/skills/**` and locks those paths (work-packages.yaml:317-318, 336-337) although nothing there is under version control. Resolution: use `grep -rliI` (or `git grep --no-index`) for the mirror assertion specifically, keeping `git grep` everywhere it inspects tracked files.

The package DAG drops a cross-package task dependency the task list declares. `wp-skills` states `Implements tasks 0.1-0.3, 3.1-3.12, 4.2` (work-packages.yaml:177) but declares `depends_on: [wp-empirical]` (line 180). Task 4.2 declares `Dependencies: 2.7, 0.1` (tasks.md:242), and task 2.7 is inside wp-coordinator (tasks 2.1-2.10). wp-frontend handles the symmetric case correctly — task 4.1 also depends on 2.7 and wp-frontend declares `depends_on: [wp-coordinator]` (line 249) — so the omission in wp-skills is an inconsistency, not a deliberate relaxation. This is load-bearing rather than cosmetic: the file task 4.2 edits, `skills/tests/agent-coordinator/test_kanban_viz_endpoints.py`, inserts `agent-coordinator/` on `sys.path` and imports coordinator source (lines 35-40 of that file), so in wp-skills' isolated worktree it runs against the *unmodified* coordinator while asserting the new roster, and the two packages can land mutually inconsistent kanban fixtures with both gates green. Resolution: either add `wp-coordinator` to wp-skills' `depends_on`, or move task 4.2 into wp-coordinator (its natural home — 2.7 already owns the coordinator-side twin of that fixture).

A tracked template enumerating gemini falls outside every package's write scope and every gate. `git grep -lIi gemini -- openspec ':!openspec/changes' ':!openspec/specs' ':!openspec/roadmaps'` returns three files: `openspec/config.yaml` (covered by task 5.4), `openspec/schemas/consensus-report.schema.json` (covered by task 3.5), and `openspec/schemas/feature-workflow/templates/session-log.md`, which is covered by nothing. Line 52 reads `| Agent Type | <!-- claude, codex, gemini, other --> |` — a template that tells a human to record `gemini` as a live agent type, which is squarely inside D6's scope rule ('anything that instructs a human or a script'), yet it is absent from design.md's In-scope user-facing set and from the 12-file 'docs, templates' row. No package can write it: wp-skills' write_allow names only the two individual schema files under `openspec/schemas/`, and wp-docs-finalize's names only `openspec/config.yaml`. Because no gate greps `openspec/schemas/feature-workflow/`, nothing fails — the file simply survives as stale roster guidance. Resolution: add it to task 5.4's file list and to wp-docs-finalize's write_allow, or record it explicitly in the D6 deferred set so the omission is a decision rather than an oversight.

Revision-1 task numbers survive in *live* (non-historical) sections of design.md, where they now point at the wrong work. These are outside the explicitly-labeled round-1 resolution table, so they are not covered by the 'historical record' disclaimer: design.md:312 'Tasks 2.1-2.4 may invoke these CLIs with real prompts' — the empirical tasks are now 1.1-1.3, while 2.1-2.4 are the coordinator config tasks, so the operator-authorization block grants live-billing authority to the wrong tasks and withholds it from the ones that need it; design.md:316 '> Populated by Phase 2' — the empirical table is populated by Phase 1; design.md:48 'task 8.1 deletes the wrapper' — now task 2.8; design.md:71 'install.sh rewrites them (task 10.1)' — now task 6.1. The E-table's own 'Task' column (lines 290-297) was correctly renumbered to 1.1/1.2/1.3, which is what makes the surrounding prose read as an oversight rather than a convention. The authorization mismatch is the one with teeth: task 1.4's human checkpoint asks a reviewer to confirm billed calls were made under an authorization paragraph that names different tasks. Resolution: renumber the four references.

Task 5.6 does not name the file its gate greps. The task says 'Document the optional `~/.grok/config.toml` `[skills] paths` setup as operator-level, citing https://docs.x.ai/build/features/skills-plugins-marketplaces' (tasks.md:285-286) with no target path, while wp-docs-finalize asserts `git grep -q 'docs.x.ai/build/features/skills-plugins-marketplaces' -- docs/` (work-packages.yaml:357). I confirmed the URL currently exists only in `openspec/changes/add-agy-grok-pi-harnesses/contracts/roster.md` and the spec delta, not under `docs/`, so the gate does require a new or edited file there. Two failure modes: an implementer who documents it in a SKILL.md or in `agent-coordinator/README.md` satisfies the task and fails the gate; and if they create a *new* file under `docs/` without `git add`-ing it, `git grep` (index/tracked-files only) still reports nothing. Resolution: name the target file in task 5.6 — `docs/skills-workflow.md` is the natural home given 5.6 already depends on 5.3 — and note the file must be staged before the gate runs.
